section.title: Introduction
section.simpara: Papillon Journey is an online JRPG and a training platform where players sharpen their systems and software engineering skills through quests, challenges, mini-games, and immersive storylines.
This document presents our vision for the project: what it is, why it matters, and how we intend to make it succeed.

section.title: Purpose
section.simpara: Formal and model-driven approaches to software development emerged in the 1960s–1980s through close collaboration between academia and industries operating under extreme safety and reliability demands — the earliest being defence, aerospace, nuclear power, and railway signalling. Their use broadened during the 1990s–2000s to other life-critical (automotive, medical devices) and high-stakes domains (finance, hardware design). They are now gradually entering mainstream software engineering, finding applications in cloud infrastructure, telecommunications, blockchain, and cybersecurity.
Papillon Journey seizes this momentum and tackles three persistent barriers to broader adoption:

listitem.simpara: Limited exposure. The historical confinement of these approaches to high-assurance niches has unintentionally reinforced the misconception that they are irrelevant to the daily concerns of most software professionals. Demonstrating their power through large-scale, open-source initiatives in web, mobile, and game development will help dispel this view. That is why Papillon Journey will be cross-platform — playable directly in a web browser or via native applications on smartphones, tablets, and PCs.

Fragmented tooling. Companies favour tools that integrate smoothly into existing workflows. Those supporting formal methods — narrowly specialised and rarely interoperable — often fail to do so. Chrysal Studio, the research subproject of Papillon Journey, will explore and prototype an integrated engineering environment to change that. We will start building with the patchwork of disjointed tools available today, transitioning progressively to Chrysal Studio, until it can fully sustain both itself and the game.

Inverted pedagogy. Children learn to add and multiply long before they ever hear of ring theory — and only if they choose to. Yet formal modelling is typically taught the other way around: heavy on theory, light on practice, and illustrated with simplistic ‘toy examples’ that bear little resemblance to the challenges encountered in industry. Fusing the experience of a JRPG (for example, Final Fantasy) with that of a training platform (such as Coursera) without breaking immersion is no small feat. One thing is certain, though: learners will spend most of their time practising. The very nature of JRPGs will steer us away from the pitfall of inverted pedagogy.

section.simpara: For Papillon Journey to be a living example of what it teaches, it must be libre: open for study, contribution, and adaptation, provided derivatives remain libre. Not only because we value freedom, but also to raise the visibility of formal modelling techniques — through a transparent, participatory, and engaging real-world use case accessible across various devices.

section.title: Stakeholders and value propositions
section.simpara: Value propositions evolve alongside the people they serve. As their goals, challenges, and expectations shift, some facets are reinvented and others phased out. Even so, certain core needs persist — and it is these that keep a project relevant over time. Below, we outline those that matter most to our stakeholders and map them to value propositions. For a deeper dive, see papillon-docs-3.

section.title: Video game players
section.simpara:
Training is future-oriented: the time and effort invested in it aim to unlock later payoffs — a job, promotion, career pivot, or proficiency. There is no such thing as training for the sake of it. The appeal of gaming, on the other hand, is precisely a break from that logic. Players expect games to provide a brief window in their day through which they can set aside future concerns and fully enjoy the present moment. An experience that fails to honour this misses the whole point.
This is why Papillon Journey will be, above all, fun.

It will be a play-anywhere-anytime game by design. The web version will render 2D isometric visuals with vector-based, hand-drawn art that looks great and performs beautifully on everything from smartphones to desktops. Where hardware permits, native editions on Windows, Android, iOS/iPadOS, and HarmonyOS will elevate the experience with enhanced 2.5D graphics, richer lighting, and added depth. Progress will synchronise across all platforms, so players can switch between devices without friction.

Players will be able to help each other without having to be online at the same time. They will share resources, discoveries, and strategies through dedicated in-world places (for example, community shops, noticeboards, or guild halls). They will also be able to compare performances on selected challenges and improve their rank over time.

For specific mini-games, players will be able to compete live in short, self-contained sessions accessed through dedicated in-game areas. These activities will be designed to be optional, quick to join, and rewarding even in brief play windows.

section.title: Software engineering learners
section.simpara: The initial training of a software engineer reaches a satisfying end once they have the skills to turn software ideas into working, maintainable systems. Teamwork is one of them, as most systems are built through collaborative effort. Continuing education then becomes a pursuit of mastery and specialisation.
Papillon Journey will support both stages of the learners’ journey in two mutually reinforcing ways:

listitem.simpara: Software engineering fundamentals will be woven into the gameplay, so learners can grow through playful practice of project and product management, UX design, specification, development, verification, and validation. As playable characters level up, their progression will mirror the learner’s growth as a software engineer, with the endgame aligning with the completion of the initial learning journey.

For players who discover a new or renewed passion for what they learned in-game, the game’s codebase itself will serve as a playground for deeper mastery. They will be encouraged to contribute to it or adapt it into something different, supported by strong documentation, welcoming contributor workflows, and a community culture that can grow around the project and its derivatives.

section.simpara: Teaching is one of the fastest ways to learn. Papillon Journey will let learners gradually step into educator roles by creating and sharing their own storylines, quests, and training content. This will be enabled through a modding system (including player-built downloadable content) designed to reward clarity, creativity, and helpfulness — and to make peer-to-peer knowledge transmission a natural part of the game.

section.title: Software engineering educators
section.simpara: Papillon Journey will be designed to be forked and adapted. Clear documentation, predictable architecture, and curriculum-friendly extension points will help educators tailor the game to their teaching goals while keeping learners immersed.

As adoption grows, the project will seek partnerships with recognised institutions and, where aligned, established game studios or franchises. Such collaborations can add legitimacy (which learners often value), broaden reach, and accelerate content quality — while remaining compatible with the project’s libre commitments.
